title: Using tissue removed during routine surgery, together with donors' genetic information, to understand how genetic differences affect the way human tissues respond to disease and treatment
summary:
Background and study aims
Many diseases are influenced by small differences in our DNA. Large genetic studies have identified thousands of genetic variants linked to disease, but researchers often do not know exactly which genes and cell types are affected. This makes it harder to develop new treatments. The Multiscale Analysis of Surgical Tissue (MAST) study aims to improve understanding of how genetic differences affect human tissues at the molecular and cellular level. By studying tissue samples collected during surgery and comparing them with genetic information, researchers hope to identify genes, biological pathways and potential drug targets that may help improve the diagnosis and treatment of a wide range of diseases. 

Who can participate?
Adults aged 18 years and over who are scheduled to undergo surgery at a participating study site and are able to provide written informed consent may be eligible to take part. 

What does the study involve?
Participants will be asked to provide written informed consent before taking part. The study mainly uses tissue that would otherwise be discarded after surgery. Depending on the type of operation and the participant’s consent, researchers may also collect up to two small additional tissue samples during the operation and/or a small blood sample of up to 4 mL.
The collected samples will be analysed in laboratories using a range of molecular and genetic techniques. Researchers will study gene activity, proteins, metabolites and other cellular features, and compare these findings with participants’ genetic information. No experimental treatment, drug or medical device is being tested, and taking part will not change a participant’s usual clinical care. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants are unlikely to receive any direct medical benefit from taking part. However, the information collected may help researchers better understand how diseases develop and may support the development of new medicines, diagnostic tests and treatments in the future.
Risks are expected to be low. The study mainly uses tissue that would otherwise be discarded. Participants who choose to provide additional tissue samples or a blood sample may experience minor discomfort, bruising, bleeding or a small risk of infection associated with sample collection. 

Where is the study run from?
The study is run from Multiscale Laboratories Limited, London, United Kingdom. The first participating centre is Royal Surrey County Hospital in Guildford, England. 

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
December 2026 to December 2036. 

Who is funding the study?
Multiscale Laboratories Limited (UK). 

Who is the main contact?
Dr Jonathan Millar, Multiscale Laboratories Limited 
jm@multiscalelabs.com

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Aged 18 years or older at the time of consent
2. Expected to undergo a surgical procedure at a participating site from which tissue specimens will be available
3. Capacity and willingness to provide written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Current enrolment in a clinical study whose protocol prohibits co-enrolment
2. Known or suspected infection with:
2.1. Any hazard group 4 biological agent on the Advisory Committee on Dangerous Pathogens (ACDP) Approved List of biological agents
2.2. Active Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex infection
2.3. A transmissible spongiform encephalopathy (including CJD or variant CJD), or recognised increased risk of one as defined in ACDP TSE Subgroup guidance
2.4. Any other hazard group 3 agent transmissible by routes other than blood and body fluids (for example Yersinia pestis, dengue virus, West Nile virus), or any agent excluded by local health and safety guidance
